nodes.label: Web Client
nodes.description: Browser or mobile app making HTTP requests

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.description: Routes requests, enforces rate limits, strips headers

nodes.label: Auth Service
nodes.description: Issues and validates JWT tokens against user credentials

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.description: Core business logic handling CRUD operations

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.description: Primary relational store for users, orders, and resources

nodes.label: Redis Cache
nodes.description: Holds hot query results and session data in memory

nodes.label: Message Queue
nodes.description: Buffers async tasks so the app server can respond immediately

nodes.label: Background Worker
nodes.description: Processes queued jobs like email sends and report generation

nodes.label: Email Provider
nodes.description: External SMTP service for transactional emails

layers.title: The Basic Request Loop
layers.explanation: A client talks to a server that reads and writes a database — this is the irreducible skeleton of any REST API. Every other piece in the system exists because this simple loop hits limits at scale or complexity.

layers.title: Who Are You?
layers.explanation: An auth service sits between the gateway and the database to verify identity before any request touches business logic. Without it, every endpoint is public and anyone can read or mutate anyone else's data.

layers.title: Stop Asking the Database the Same Question
layers.explanation: A Redis cache gives the app server a fast in-memory layer so repeated reads hit RAM instead of disk. The database is the bottleneck in almost every web app, and caching is the cheapest way to relieve it.

layers.title: Do It Later
layers.explanation: A message queue lets the app server hand off slow work and respond to the client immediately. Sending an email or generating a PDF doesn't need to block a 200ms API response — so we decouple the trigger from the execution.

layers.title: The Outside World
layers.explanation: The background worker connects to an external email provider to actually deliver transactional messages. This is where the system's boundary meets a third-party service it doesn't control, introducing retries and failure handling.
